name: master-suite
product: Signal Studio — Notes, Tasks and Timeline as one running application on one world of data

notes.master: _gate-suite.html is written by tools/wrap.mjs from master.html. master.html is page CONTENT — no doctype, html, head or body — because the published artifact supplies the skeleton. Nothing can open it as a file without one, so every gate opens the wrapped copy.
notes.states: The suite answers ?state=<product>.<state> as well as its own ?p= and ?state=. The compound form exists so a toolchain that can set one parameter can reach all three products. Folded from the full space: Tasks ships 6 states, Notes 10, Timeline 14 — thirty in all. The eight here are the ones a defect would be found in; the folds are recorded in brief.md. A DOT and not a colon: a state name is also a filename, and the shot harness names every frame after its state — a colon collapsed forty frames into three on Windows without erroring. notes.review ADDED 2026-09-02: the one state in the suite that scrolled sideways at 390 was the one the gate never walked.
notes.variants: paper and ink are Timeline's two ratified grounds. Tasks and Notes have no ground decision and ignore ?v= at these values, which is correct: they are the ink-floor products and the ground decision was only ever Timeline's.
notes.ladders: sizes and spaces are EMPTY DELIBERATELY, and this is a known gap, not an oversight. The source ladders read the stylesheets, and this artefact carries three products with three separately declared and separately ratified ladders — Timeline invented its own material system by name in its lock. One config cannot hold three. Each product is held to its OWN ladders by tools/gates.mjs, which repoints the three engagements' own audits at this file; this config covers what is genuinely cross-product: the palette, the families, the weights, contrast, targets, radii, motion and leading, at five viewports across all three surfaces.
notes.palette: Indigo deep #4338ca is the indigo ramp one step darker. It is declared in both the Tasks and Notes shells as --indigo-deep and was part of the three-colour lock's own reading of itself from the first round of both engagements. STATUS COLOURS, added 2026-08-27 on the founder's explicit instruction after the monochrome version was reviewed and found unreadable: “the coloured dots aren’t noticeable at all”. Three hues carry lane STATE and nothing else — amber #a16207 for Review, orange #c2410c for Waiting, green #15803d for Done — with To do on ink and In progress on the existing indigo. They are deliberately deep rather than bright: every one clears 4.9:1 on white, which is AA for text and well past the 3:1 the non-text rule asks of an indicator, so the system gains meaning without gaining loudness. This spends the four-colour lock. It was raised as a founder’s call before it was spent, and it was spent because the founder made it. REVISED 2026-08-27 after the founder reviewed the tints and called them “a bit dirty” — which was exactly right and measurable: every wash was derived by diluting the DOT colour, the dot has to be dark to carry contrast, and diluting a dark colour toward white destroys its chroma. The washes measured chroma 7–13, which is grey with a faint cast: a beige grey, a muddy pink, a sickly green. A wash is now its own colour, taken from a BRIGHT hue at a higher alpha — chroma 17–36, which reads as a clean tint. Each dot is a bright fill with a deep rim of the same hue, so it reads as its colour and still has a defined edge. That is also how Review can be a real yellow: #eab308 is unmistakably yellow at 1.9:1 and could never be an indicator on its own, but rimmed in #a16207 at 4.9:1 the EDGE carries the definition and the fill carries the meaning. INDIGO ON INK #818cf8 added 2026-08-27 from the founder's own rail-redesign session (Turn 2, direction 1a), which specifies it as the dark-mode accent. #4f46e5 is the accent on paper and is too dark to be an accent ON the ink rail; this is the same indigo lifted for a dark ground, exactly as --on-ink-* lifts ink. It is spent only on the active product tile, its glyph and its label — the design's own rule is that nothing else in the rail spends indigo.
notes.typeRamp: The union of the three products' ramps, and it is a UNION rather than a law — Timeline declares thirteen steps and gates them, Notes declares eight and gates them, Tasks declares none and its own audit has never had a ramp check. 14 is here because the Tasks card title, the most-read string on the board, is set at 14 and is on no ramp declared in that lab; 16 is here because the screen-reader live regions inherit it at a 1x1 box nobody sees. Both are recorded as observations in round 1 rather than smuggled in as law.
notes.paletteRule: Colour carries LANE STATE and nothing else: five lanes, five hues, on at rest. Everywhere else — severity, hierarchy, emphasis — is still ink density, weight and fill, and a finding that proposes colour for any of those is out of scope. The status system was built after the monochrome version was reviewed and rejected by the founder; the palette above already includes it, so it is not a violation to report.
